# STY021 `too-many-arguments`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="info" text="opt-in" />

A procedure has more than 8 dummy arguments.

## Why

Long argument lists are easy to call with arguments in the wrong order (same types, positional
calls) and usually mean that several arguments belong together: group them in a derived type.

## Reported

```fortran
subroutine flux(q, ni, nj, nk, ng, dx, dy, dz, gamma, r)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
subroutine flux(q, grid, gas)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[STY021] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = STY021` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `S902` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
